ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZdoNlg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDEzWI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 33, "title": "Allocate and present owned immersive XRWebGLLayer framebuffers", "body": "## Problem

At `dev` revision `fd71ffdff3c8857de4a326188fdf227eea829db8`, `XRWebGLLayer.framebuffer` is always null, dimensions follow the application canvas, `framebufferScaleFactor` is ignored, and antialiasing follows context attributes. Depth, stencil and alpha initialization do not allocate independent resources. The class also lacks `XRLayer` inheritance. See [layers.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/fd71ffdff3c8857de4a326188fdf227eea829db8/src/polyfill/api/layers.ts).

Applications cannot rely on independent XR render targets or requested rendering options. Existing rendering evidence demonstrates default-framebuffer pixels, rather than the missing resource contract.

## Expected outcome

Provide usable owned immersive framebuffers, their initialization and presentation, for Quest 3 `immersive-vr`, Quest MR and Android `immersive-ar`, through WebGL1 and WebGL2. Preserve inline default-framebuffer behavior. This Device API functionality requires no feature descriptor, including no `layers` request.

Application drawing must reach the VR preview and AR room/tablet with correct view allocation, alpha and color handling. Virtual display dimensions remain emulator policy.

## Context

Start from and target `dev`. Inspect `api/layers.ts`, `api/runtime.ts`, `webgl.ts`, `EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `ARScene.ts`, and `src/types/polyfill.ts`. Runtime presentation currently assumes the application's canvas; `XRWebGLBinding` also constructs an internal `XRWebGLLayer`. Update these dependencies together so allocation does not break projection/quad presentation.

Use [Device CRD 2026-06-09 §11](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#layers), [WebIDL 622910c](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs), and [WPT e185958](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/tree/e1859580b5fcf74940a18d2f783296b4961035e3/webxr): the constructor, framebuffer scaling/identity/drawing/opacity/stencil and viewport files. WPT uses native fake-device setup; adapt applicable assertions to real extension sessions and record differences. The current five-file WPT runner does not execute these cases.

All 32 existing Issues/PRs are closed. [Issue #11's outcome](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/11#issuecomment-6203709987) explicitly retains unfinished framebuffer work. PR #32 reports Chromium 156.0.8078.4 implementation-stage success, without new official-application or Firefox execution. This task addresses that remaining gap.

Retain and correct two prior assumptions in the Issue/PR record:

- Original: V24 accepted a zero-width right-eye viewport when stereo preview was disabled. Correction: exposed views need usable, nonoverlapping viewports, corroborated by pinned WPT `xrWebGLLayer_viewports.https.html`. Preserve the preview preference through presentation policy instead of suppressing an exposed API viewport.
- Original: the inventory broadly describes native opaque resources as unenforceable. Correction: owned allocation and ordinary API protections remain actionable. [Mozilla's MAIN-world documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/content_scripts#world) supports the narrower inference that page interference prevents claiming hostile-code-proof native isolation. Document any concrete bypass, application impact and alternatives; do not use this limitation to omit framebuffer support.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement `XRLayer` inheritance and readonly framebuffer identity/dimensions. Convert all six initialization members with their pinned defaults: antialias/depth/alpha true, stencil/ignoreDepthValues false, scale 1. Cover omitted/null dictionaries, inherited ordered getters, boolean conversion, finite-double conversion and propagation of conversion failures before allocation.
- [ ] Immersive layers own distinct, stable, non-null framebuffer objects in the supplied context. Allocate meaningful depth/stencil and RGB/RGBA resources, implement real antialiasing when reported, and apply a documented bounded scale/rounding policy. Demonstrate different allocations at scales 0.5 and 1; cover finite nonpositive/extreme inputs without unsafe allocations. Inline remains null and reflects actual default-buffer properties.
- [ ] Preserve constructor `TypeError` conversion failures, `InvalidStateError` for ended sessions/lost contexts/incompatible immersive contexts, and `OperationError` for allocation failure. Roll back partial allocations. Report `ignoreDepthValues=true` while compositor depth consumption is absent; depth testing inside the application framebuffer must still work.
- [ ] Present completed application rendering through the virtual display, including antialias resolve, premultiplied alpha and absence of extra gamma conversion. Separate owned storage dimensions from application canvas writes. Document resize/DPR behavior; newly created layers use current recommendations. Support main-thread OffscreenCanvas contexts accepted by the API, without assuming they are DOM elements.
- [ ] Produce positive integer, bounded, nonoverlapping viewports for every exposed eye, including odd target widths and both stereo-preview settings. Android remains monoscopic. Foreign-session or stale views reject appropriately. Keep projections consistent with allocated view regions.
- [ ] Clear owned buffers before frame callbacks and implement ordinary opacity/lifetime protections: attachment inspection/mutation/deletion errors, unavailable framebuffer status and drawing outside the owning animation callback, and availability during it. Preserve unrelated GL state and errors, including distinct WebGL2 read/draw bindings. State any evidenced native-enforcement limitation precisely.
- [ ] Preserve reusable layers across base-layer replacement and legacy/projection/quad transitions. Release all session-owned allocations on end, including never-submitted layers; handle context loss and shutdown inside callbacks without later presentation or leaks. Demonstrate subsequent session creation succeeds.
- [ ] Extend the existing browser harness with targeted resource, pixel and lifecycle cases across all three immersive configurations, WebGL1/2 and inline. Demonstrate depth/stencil behavior independently of default-context attachments, alpha true/false, scaling, per-eye pixels, clearing, resize and state restoration. Update fixtures that currently draw to null to bind the advertised framebuffer; retain separate default-output presentation observations. Preserve existing projection/quad pixels and accurately distinguish the known Three.js depth-disabled client failure from successful rendering.
- [ ] The Coordinator performs implementation-stage `npm run build` and `npm run test:browser` with these additions, recording revision/file hashes, browser/tool versions, actual outcomes, failures and skips. Update the capability inventory and inspect generated bundle changes. Record source-backed requirement corrections with original assumption, correction and rationale; no human approval or independent AI re-review is required. Preserve meaningful acceptance.

## Optional validation

Run the pinned, unmodified WebXR Samples immersive VR page against the new resource path. Official Three.js r186 `WebXRManager` consumes layer dimensions, framebuffer and viewports; use it for additional compatibility evidence where applicable. Record exact executed sources and distinguish custom fixtures from official applications. Firefox runtime coverage and remaining modules remain separate goal work.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

Evaluation baseline: `fd71ffdff3c8857de4a326188fdf227eea829db8`.
